subject: Performance mapping & next steps — FintechCo trial
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@fintechco.com>, Samir Patel <samir@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Performance mapping & next steps — FintechCo trial

Hi Olivia / Samir,

Thanks again for taking time today — good first call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything in one thread. High-level takeaways from our conversation: 

- Primary pain: unpredictable latency for live scoring during peak hours (spiky bursts cause user-visible lag).
- Current stack: in-house model endpoints behind K8s + custom queuing, using a 7B model in FP16; no KV cache today.
- Success criteria you called out: p95 inference latency <= 250–300 ms for streaming token-first-response, support for ~250 concurrent user sessions with instant interactive UX, and ability to sustain 10k tokens/sec aggregated at peak.
- Security: VPC peering + strict IP allowlist, sample data can be shared via SFTP (PII redacted).

Proposed next steps / owners:
1) Redwood to run a focused perf plan: micro-benchmarks (latency p95/median), streaming-first-byte tests, and a concurrency sweep mapped to your session pattern — Sean to run (attached: initial-inference-map.pdf). (Action: Sean / Redwood)
2) FintechCo provides a ~1k-row sample payload and a short call script for realistic prompt mixes. (Action: Olivia / Samir)
3) Redwood to create a short trial plan (3 days of tests + 1-day results review) and an initial cost estimate for the trial capacity. (Action: Marissa / Diego)
4) Schedule a 60-min technical deep dive after we have the sample data (target next week).

Can you confirm the p95 target (250 ms is the preferred goal, you mentioned 300 ms as acceptable), and whether the 250 concurrent sessions figure is peak simultaneous or average active sessions? Once I have that, we’ll finalize the load profile.

Attachments: initial-inference-map.pdf (diagram + perf checklist).

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Sun, Apr 18, 2027 at 3:02 PM Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Thanks again for taking time today — good first call. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have everything in one thread.

Thanks Diego — this is exactly what we needed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Confirm p95 goal: our product team will prioritize hitting <= 250 ms for the streaming-first-byte in the interactive flow; 300 ms is our upper bound but we should aim for 250 ms.
- Concurrent sessions: 250 is peak simultaneous active users (desktop + mobile), seen for short bursts during our market close windows.
- Tokens: 10k tokens/sec is aggregated peak across all endpoints — most sessions are short (5–20 tokens) but we get heavy bursts.

I’ve attached a small sanitized sample dataset (FintechCo-trial-data-sample.csv) and a short user script describing prompt patterns. We have strict network controls — we’ll need VPC peering or an approved egress IP range for the trial.

Timeline: we’re targeting an internal sign-off for a pilot in the first week of June, so a trial/bench that finishes by late May would be ideal.

One request: can you include a rough cost estimate for the 3-day trial (GB-GPU-hours or flat fee) so we can get procurement buy-in?

Appreciate it — Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Product, Integrations | FintechCo
olivia@fintechco.com
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@fintechco.com>, Samir Patel <samir@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance mapping & next steps — Performance mapping & next steps — FintechCo trial

Thanks for the quick turnaround and sample data, Olivia. Confirming receipt of the CSV and the constraints. Next actions from Redwood: 

- Marissa will produce a short trial-run cost estimate (flat trial fee + incremental GPU-hours) — Marissa, can you share an initial ballpark by EOD tomorrow?
- Sean will draft the load profile and run an initial dry-run on our staging infra to validate the approach. Sean: focus on streaming-first-byte p95 and a concurrency sweep from 50 -> 300 sessions.
- Diego will coordinate the scheduling and sign-off items for procurement (VPC peering checklist).

Attached: redwood-trial-plan.yaml (high level test steps & acceptance criteria). Key acceptance criteria for the trial: 
- Streaming-first-byte p95 <= 250 ms for the interactive flow under 250 concurrent sessions.
- Sustained aggregated throughput >= 8k tokens/sec for 60s windows (we aim for 10k but 8k is acceptable to validate).
- No errors above 1% during steady-state tests.

If that sounds right I’ll lock in a proposed window May 24–26 for the tests (we can shift if needed).

Diego
Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance mapping & next steps — Performance mapping & next steps — FintechCo trial

Looping in with the runbook checklist and immediate asks so engineering can move quickly. Sean, can you take the perf job and deliver a first-pass report by Friday? Priorities below: 

- Test matrix: streaming-first-byte latency, end-to-end token latency, and KV-cache warm vs cold behavior.
- Concurrency sweep: 50 / 100 / 150 / 200 / 250 / 300 sessions with your session mix from the CSV.
- Long-run: 10-minute sustained burst at the requested 10k tokens/sec (we'll aim for 8k if infra limits).
- Environment: staging VPC; we'll request VPC peering and temporary allowlist from FintechCo.

Deliverables: 
- Sean: perf report (p50/p95/p99 + error rates) and a short recommendations list (batching, KV cache, quantization suggestions).
- Marissa: trial cost estimate + short procurement checklist for FintechCo.

Olivia — once Sean has the report we’ll schedule the technical deep dive to review findings and next steps.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
